{{short description|Theorem in matrix analysis}}
'''Crouzeix's conjecture''' is a problem in [[matrix analysis]] proposed by [[Michel Crouzeix]] in 2004,<ref>{{Cite journal|last=Crouzeix|first=Michel|date=2004-04-01|title=Bounds for Analytical Functions of Matrices|journal=Integral Equations and Operator Theory|volume=48|issue=4|pages=461–477|doi=10.1007/s00020-002-1188-6|s2cid=121371601|issn=0378-620X}}</ref> and it can be stated as follows:

: <math>\|f(A)\| \le 2 \sup_{z\in W(A)} |f(z)|,</math>

where the set <math>W(A)</math> is the [[field of values]] of a ''n''×''n'' (i.e. [[square matrix|square]]) complex matrix <math>A</math>  and <math>f</math> is a complex function that is [[Holomorphic function|analytic]] in the interior of <math>W(A)</math> and continuous up to the boundary of <math>W(A)</math>.  Slightly reformulated, the conjecture can also be stated as follows: for all square complex matrices <math>A</math> and all complex polynomials <math>p</math>:

: <math>\|p(A)\| \le 2 \sup_{z\in W(A)} |p(z)|</math>

holds, where the norm on the left-hand side is the spectral operator 2-norm.

== History ==
'''Crouzeix's theorem''', proved in 2007, states that:<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Crouzeix |first=Michel |date=2007-03-15 |title=Numerical range and functional calculus in Hilbert space |journal=Journal of Functional Analysis |volume=244 |issue=2 |pages=668–690 |doi=10.1016/j.jfa.2006.10.013 |doi-access=free}}</ref>
: <math>\|f(A)\| \le 11.08 \sup_{z\in W(A)} |f(z)|</math>

(the constant <math>11.08</math>  is independent of the matrix [[dimension (mathematics)|dimension]], thus transferable to infinite-dimensional settings).

Michel Crouzeix and Cesar Palencia proved in 2017 that the result holds for <math>1+\sqrt{2}</math>,<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Crouzeix|first1=Michel|last2=Palencia|first2=Cesar|date=2017-06-07|title=The Numerical Range is a <math>(1+\sqrt2)</math>-Spectral Set|journal= SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications |volume=38|issue=2|pages=649–655|doi=10.1137/17M1116672}}</ref> improving the original constant of <math>11.08</math>. More recently, dimension-dependent improvements have been obtained: Malman, Mashreghi, O'Loughlin and Ransford showed that for each fixed dimension <math>N</math> there exists a constant <math>C_N < 1+\sqrt{2}</math> such that the inequality holds for all <math>N\times N</math> matrices.<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Malman |first1=Bartosz |last2=Mashreghi |first2=Javad |last3=O&#39;Loughlin |first3=Ryan |last4=Ransford |first4=Thomas |title=On the Crouzeix ratio for <math>N\times N</math> matrices |eprint=2409.14127 |class=math.FA |year=2024}}</ref>

Related work connects the constant in Crouzeix-type inequalities to configuration constants arising from the Neumann–Poincaré operator and yields domain-dependent improvements of the Crouzeix–Palencia bound in certain settings.<ref>{{Cite journal |last1=Malman |first1=Bartosz |last2=Mashreghi |first2=Javad |last3=O&#39;Loughlin |first3=Ryan |last4=Ransford |first4=Thomas |date=2025-04-10 |title=Double-Layer Potentials, Configuration Constants, and Applications to Numerical Ranges |journal=International Mathematics Research Notices |volume=2025 |issue=8 |article-number=rnaf084 |doi=10.1093/imrn/rnaf084 |doi-access=free}}</ref>

The conjecture states that the constant can be refined to <math>2</math>.

== Special cases ==
Before the general case was resolved, the conjecture was shown to hold in several special cases. For instance, it holds for all [[normal matrices]],<ref name=":0" /> for tridiagonal 3×3 matrices with elliptic field of values centered at an [[eigenvalue]]<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Glader|first1=Christer|last2=Kurula|first2=Mikael|last3=Lindström|first3=Mikael|s2cid=43922128|title=Crouzeix's Conjecture Holds for Tridiagonal 3 x 3 Matrices with Elliptic Numerical Range Centered at an Eigenvalue|journal=SIAM Journal on Matrix Analysis and Applications|volume= 39|issue=1|pages= 346–364|date=2018-03-01|doi=10.1137/17M1110663|arxiv=1701.01365}}</ref> and for general ''n''×''n'' matrices that are nearly Jordan blocks.<ref name=":0">{{Cite journal|last1=Choi|first1=Daeshik|title=A proof of Crouzeix's conjecture for a class of matrices|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume= 438|issue=8|date=2013-04-15|pages=3247–3257|doi=10.1016/j.laa.2012.12.045|doi-access=free}}</ref>.  Furthermore, [[Anne Greenbaum]] and Michael L. Overton provided numerical support for Crouzeix's conjecture.<ref>{{Cite journal|last1=Greenbaum|first1=Anne|last2=Overton|first2=Michael L.|title=Numerical investigation of Crouzeix's conjecture|url=https://cs.nyu.edu/overton/papers/pdffiles/NumerInvestCrouzeixConj.pdf|journal=Linear Algebra and Its Applications|volume= 542|date=2017-05-04|pages=225–245|doi=10.1016/j.laa.2017.04.035|doi-access=free}}</ref>

== Proof ==

On July 27, 2026, neurosurgeon Shanmu Jin posted a preprint claiming a proof of Crouzeix's conjecture.<ref>{{Cite web
 |title=The Numerical Range Is a 2-Spectral Set
 |url=https://www.preprints.org/manuscript/202607.1919
 |last=Jin
 |first=Shanmu
 |date=2026
}}</ref> Jin reported that the proof was obtained with the assistance of [[OpenAI]]'s [[GPT-5|GPT-5.6 Sol]], after which he checked the resulting argument.<ref name="TownsendGreenbaum2026">{{Cite web
 |last1=Townsend
 |first1=Alex
 |last2=Greenbaum
 |first2=Anne
 |title=The Neurosurgery Resident Who Proved Crouzeix's Conjecture
 |url=https://alextownsend.net/essays/SIAMNews_CrouzeixConjecture.pdf
 |date=2026-08-14
 }}</ref> Greenbaum and Alex Townsend reported that they and Crouzeix had thoroughly reviewed the proof and believed it to be correct.<ref name="TownsendGreenbaum2026" />

On August 4, 2026, Emiel Lorist and Felix Schwenninger posted an independent proof of the conjecture using a different argument.<ref name="TownsendGreenbaum2026" /> They reported that [[GPT-5.6]] in its Sol variant "was used to explore proof strategies for this note".<ref>{{Cite arXiv |last1=Lorist |first1=Emiel |last2=Schwenninger |first2=Felix |title=A solution to Crouzeix's conjecture |date=2026 |class=math.CA |eprint=2608.03841}}</ref>
